newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Dock to merge with CityFront.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Dock to merge with CityFront.

text.p: Chicago Dock & Canal Trust, a real estate investment trust, said Friday it cancelled a proposed merger with Newsweb Corp. and accepted a higher bid of about $175 million by CityFront Centre LLC instead.
Under the agreement, CityFront will offer $25 for each of Chicago Dock's roughly 5.8 million shares outstanding. The price includes about $30 million in liabilities that CityFront will assume.
Chicago Dock said it paid a $3.5 million termination fee to Newsweb and reimbursed it up to $750,000 in expenses.
Newsweb, which originally offered $21 a share for Chicago Dock in September, raised its bid on Dec. 20 to $23 a share. CityFront last week raised its bid to $25 a share from $23.
Newsweb sued Cityfront in early December to protect its $21-a-share agreement to acquire Chicago Dock.

But at a hearing last week, the Circuit Court of Cook County, Ill., declined to issue a preliminary injunction against the CityFront deal. The court reserved consideration of all other claims in the litigation.
Chicago Dock also said CityFront has an agreement with Newsweb under which Newsweb will dismiss its lawsuit and vote its Chicago Dock shares in favour of CityFront merger.
The merger with CityFront is subject to approval by Chicago Dock shareholders, the trust said.

Chicago Dock said it authorised the cancellation of the special meeting of shareholders originally scheduled for Jan. 9 to consider the previous merger agreement with Newsweb. It expects to hold a new special meeting to vote on the CityFront merger in the first quarter of 1997.
Chicago Dock's stock fell 37.5 cents to $24.50 on Nasdaq.
